summary: This guide explains how families can support mental health and cognitive function in older adults, drawing on research and expert presentations from 2023-2024. It covers exercise, nutrition, social interaction, mental exercises, sleep, mental health recognition, medication management, technology use, and a safe home environment. The central message is that a caring, involved family can meaningfully improve seniors' quality of life and cognitive longevity.
one_line: A family guide to preserving elderly cognitive and mental health through activity, diet, social ties, sleep, medication management, technology, and home safety.
key_facts: The Geriatric Health Summit was held on November 10, 2023, with experts including Dr. Jennifer Rocha and Professor Lionel Simmons.
Dr. Jennifer Rocha presented research in September 2023 suggesting an active and engaged lifestyle helps preserve mental acuity.
Professor Lionel Simmons' study, dated October 15, 2023, links supportive family networks directly to better cognitive health in the elderly.
A February 2024 study by the Geriatric Society of America found that consistency and enjoyment are key to physical activities for older adults.
Dietitian Laura Bennett emphasized on March 5, 2024 a balanced diet of fish, nuts, berries, and leafy vegetables to enhance mental function and mitigate cognitive decline.
Social psychologist Dr. Mark Thompson said on January 13, 2024 that social interaction bolsters cognitive resilience, potentially delaying dementia-related symptoms.
Neurologist Dr. Anita Kapoor's research dated April 18, 2024 shows mental stimulation can significantly reduce cognitive decline.
Sleep expert Dr. Emily Hansen's study, released August 27, 2024, stresses adequate sleep and an established sleep routine for cognitive health.
Psychiatrist Dr. Samuel Lee found in September 2024 that early intervention and treatment of mental health conditions helps preserve cognitive function.
Geriatric pharmacist Maria Gonzales highlighted on December 1, 2023 the importance of a proper medication regimen for cognitive health.
Technology integration specialist Josh Anderson led a workshop on February 10, 2024 showing older adults can gain cognitive benefits from technology with proper guidance.
Occupational Therapist Helen Yi presented a case study on September 30, 2023 showing a well-structured living space positively affects seniors' cognitive function.
Families can help by organizing group activities, preparing nutritious meals, arranging visits and video calls, organizing medications, and decluttering and adding safety features at home.
